decision.summary: The Federal Reserve lowered its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to a range of 1 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate 50 basis points to 1 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed lowered the federal funds rate target to 1 percent.

changes.quote: The pace of economic activity appears to have slowed markedly, owing importantly to a decline in consumer expenditures.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that economic growth has slowed down significantly due to drops in consumer spending.

changes.quote: Business equipment spending and industrial production have weakened in recent months, and slowing economic activity in many foreign economies is damping the prospects for U.S. exports.
changes.explanation: Business investments and manufacturing are weakening, and slowing foreign economies are hurting U.S. exports.

tone_quotes.quote: The pace of economic activity appears to have slowed markedly, owing importantly to a decline in consumer expenditures.
Moreover, the intensification of financial market turmoil is likely to exert additional restraint on spending, partly by further reducing the ability of households and businesses to obtain credit.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 11.88% APR, a 50 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $2.08.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.93% and moved +4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.46% would rise by about $7.88 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $30.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 6.1%, and employers added an average of -313k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 5% over the past year (September 2008); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -2.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -7 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -2.27% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed will continue monitoring economic developments carefully to support growth and price stability.
